title: Critical cosets, unrestricted infima and coefficient bounds
statement: Let $F$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute value, with nondiscrete value group and residue characteristic $p>0$. Here $F^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] and the residue field is $F^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$. For $a,b\in F$ and $s>0$ put $S_{a,s}(F)=\{c^p-ac+e:c,e\in F,\ |pc^p|<s,\ |e|<s\}$. This is an additive subgroup. Call $C=b+S_{a,s}(F)$ critical if $0\notin C$ and $\inf_{v\in C}|v|=s$. Then $C$ is critical if and only if $|pb|<s=\inf_{c\in F}|c^p-ac+b|$. For a critical coset, $|a|\le s^{(p-1)/p}$ and every $v\in C$ satisfies $|pv|<s$. If $v\in C$, then $C=v+S_{a,s}(F)$, and $\inf_{c\in F,\ |pc^p|<s}|c^p-ac+v|=s$.

source.place: Definition before Lemma 6.1.2 and Lemma 6.1.2(i)--(ii), printed pp. 37--38; translated critical representatives.

proof.text: Write $q=|p\cdot1_F|<1$ and $P(c)=c^p-ac$. Since the residue field has characteristic $p$, $p$ is prime. Integers have norm at most $1$, and $p\mid\binom pi$ for $0<i<p$. Thus $|(c+d)^p-c^p-d^p|\le q\max(|c|,|d|)^p$. For admissible $c,d$ this error has norm $<s$, and $q|c+d|^p<s$. Therefore $(P(c)+e)+(P(d)+e^\prime)=P(c+d)+(e+e^\prime-((c+d)^p-c^p-d^p))$ is in $S_{a,s}(F)$. Zero is in it. For inverses use $-c$; the error $-c^p-(-c)^p$ is zero for odd $p$, and is $-2c^2$ for $p=2$, of norm $<s$. This proves the additive-subgroup assertion, also when $q=0$.

source.place: Definition before Lemma 6.1.2, printed p. 37; explicit binomial and inverse calculations.

proof.text: Put $S=S_{a,s}(F)$ and $f_v(c)=P(c)+v$. For every $v\in C$, the subgroup identity gives $C=v+S$. Moreover $0\in C$ if and only if some member has norm $<s$: subtract that member using $c=0$ in $S$. If $0\notin C$, every admissible $f_v(c)$ has norm at least $s$; hence $|f_v(c)+e|=|f_v(c)|$ for $|e|<s$. Consequently $\inf_{w\in C}|w|=\inf_{q|c|^p<s}|f_v(c)|$. Both sets are nonempty and bounded below by zero, so these are ordinary real infima. This proves the asserted restricted infimum for every representative of a critical coset.

source.place: Definition before Lemma 6.1.2, printed p. 37, removing the small error term and changing representatives.

proof.text:
Assume $C$ is critical. To prove the coefficient bound, suppose $|a|>s^{(p-1)/p}$ and set $A=|a|^{p/(p-1)}>s$. Choose $v\in C$ with $|v|<A$ and $q|v|<s$; such a choice follows from $\inf|C|=s$ and $q<1$ (if $q>0$, use the upper bound $\min(A,s/q)>s$; if $q=0$, use $A$). Since $v

e0$. Since $|v|<A$, we have $|v|^{p-1}<|a|^p$; hence $|c|^p=|v|^p/|a|^p<|v|$ and $|c|^{p-1}<|a|$. Thus $|f_v(c)|=|c|^p<|v|=|ac|$. Apply [lem-trf-binomial-root-correction] with constant coefficient $v$ to obtain a root $z$ with $|z|=|v/a|$. Thus $q|z|^p<q|v|<s$ when $q>0$, and it is zero when $q=0$. Hence $P(z)=-v\in S$, contradicting $0
otin C$. This proves $|a|\le s^{(p-1)/p}$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.2(ii), printed pp. 37–38; small-root argument also treats an attained infimum.

proof.text: For critical $C$ and $v\in C$, if $|v|=s$ then $q|v|<s$. If $|v|>s$, step 2 supplies $c$ with $q|c|^p<s$ and $|f_v(c)|<|v|$, so $|P(c)|=|v|>s$. If $|c|^p\le s$, then step 3 gives $|ac|\le s^{(p-1)/p}s^{1/p}=s$, contradicting $|P(c)|>s$. Hence $|c|^p>s$. The coefficient bound now gives $|ac|\le s^{(p-1)/p}|c|<|c|^p$. Thus $|v|=|P(c)|=|c|^p$, and $q|v|=q|c|^p<s$. This includes $v=b$ and proves the strict $p$-bound for every representative, also when $q=0$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.2(i), direct implication, printed p. 38; representative bound assembled from the coefficient estimate of (ii).

proof.text: For critical $C$, the unrestricted infimum is at most the restricted one, which is $s$. If $|f_b(c)|<s$, $c$ cannot be admissible by step 2. Thus $q|c|^p\ge s$, so $q>0$ and $|c|^p>s$. The coefficient bound of step 3 gives $|ac|<|c|^p$. Since $|f_b(c)|<s<|c|^p$, it follows that $|b|=|c|^p$, contradicting $q|b|<s$ from step 4. Thus every unrestricted value has norm at least $s$, and its infimum is $s$.

Conversely assume $q|b|<s=\inf_{c\in F}|f_b(c)|$, so $|b|\ge s>0$ and $f_b$ has no root in $F$. If $|b|=s$, $c=0$ realizes the restricted infimum. Otherwise fix $s<r<|b|$ and choose $c$ with $|f_b(c)|<r$, using the unrestricted infimum. Suppose $q|c|^p\ge s$. Then $q>0$ and $|c|^p\ge s/q>|b|$. Since $|f_b(c)|<|b|$, cancellation forces $|ac|=|c|^p>|b|$, so $c\ne0$ because $|c|^p>|b|>0$. Dividing $|ac|=|c|^p$ by $|c|$ gives $|c|^{p-1}=|a|$, and $|f_b(c)|<|ac|$. Now [lem-trf-binomial-root-correction] produces a root of $f_b$, a contradiction. Thus $c$ is admissible. For every $t>s$ choose $r$ with $s<r<\min(t,|b|)$; the admissible $c$ just obtained has $|f_b(c)|<t$. Hence the restricted infimum is at most every $t>s$ and therefore at most $s$, while the unrestricted lower bound makes it at least $s$. Also every $f_b(c)+e$, with $c$ admissible and $|e|<s$, has the same norm as $f_b(c)$, so $0\notin C$ and $\inf|C|=s$. This proves criticality, without using the coefficient bound before criticality is known.
